blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At its best, the British approach to customer experience is a signature — a recognisable blend of politeness, patience, discretion and quiet competence that customers around the world associate instinctively with Britishness. It is not, as cliché sometimes suggests, a performance of charm. It is a disciplined balance of genuine care and practical efficiency, delivered without announcement.

The senior leader's role is to protect this signature across every touchpoint and every generation of the team. New technologies arrive, customer expectations shift, cheaper rivals appear. Through all of this, the signature holds only if the culture actively defends it — by training new staff in the tone as carefully as in the product, by rewarding those who embody it even when the numbers do not show it, and by intervening quickly when someone senior breaks it for the sake of a short-term result.

Only when that care is sustained, year after year, does the signature become truly valuable. Only then does it become the kind of quiet competitive advantage that cannot be copied by a competitor with a better algorithm and a lower price.

items.q: According to the text, the British approach to customer experience is best understood as…
options: a recognisable signature blending care and efficiency
items.why: "the British approach to customer experience is a signature — a recognisable blend of politeness… and quiet competence."

items.q: How does the text say the signature should be delivered?
items.why: "a disciplined balance of genuine care and practical efficiency, delivered without announcement."

items.q: The phrase "rewarding those who embody it even when the numbers do not show it" suggests that…
options: metrics are the only fair basis for reward
staff should be paid more than the numbers allow
reward should be delayed until results improve
the right behaviour should be recognised regardless of short-term metrics
items.why: Inferência: o autor defende recompensar a conduta certa mesmo sem retorno imediato nos indicadores.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: The signature grows valuable only when sustained over years.
Protecting customer experience is a leadership responsibility.
Culture must actively defend the signature.
A superior algorithm and a lower price are enough to replicate the signature.
items.why: Inferência: o texto termina dizendo justamente que é a vantagem que NÃO pode ser copiada por algoritmo e preço.

items.q: What does the final paragraph imply about the value of the signature?
options: It accrues slowly, through consistency maintained year after year
It depends mainly on beating rivals on price
It appears instantly once the right process is written down
It fades as the organisation grows
items.why: Inferência: "Only when that care is sustained, year after year, does the signature become truly valuable" — o valor vem da consistência ao longo do tempo.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry conduzindo a sessão de liderança sobre como proteger a experiência do cliente na expansão. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, let me set the frame for today. We are going from three offices to twelve, and the thing I lose sleep over is not the logistics. It is whether the experience a client gets in office number eleven feels the same as the one they get here in London.

Because that consistency is the whole point. Clients cannot always articulate what they value — but they notice the moment it slips. A returned call a little slower than usual, a tone that is polite but hurried. None of it shows on a dashboard, and yet it is precisely what they remember.

So here is what I am asking of every one of you. Train the new joiners in the tone as carefully as in the product. Protect the people who embody it, even in the quarters when their numbers look ordinary. And if someone senior ever cuts a corner on the experience to hit a target, intervene straight away — do not wait for me.

Only when we defend this thing deliberately, in twelve offices as we did in one, does it stay a signature. Lose it, and we are just another firm competing on price.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Harry say worries him most about the expansion?
options: The logistics of moving staff around
Whether the client experience stays consistent across all offices
The cost of opening nine new offices
items.why: "whether the experience a client gets in office number eleven feels the same as the one they get here in London."

items.q: According to Harry, why is dashboard data insufficient here?
options: What clients notice and remember does not always show on a dashboard
The metrics are updated too slowly
items.why: "None of it shows on a dashboard, and yet it is precisely what they remember."

items.q: What does Harry ask people to do if a senior colleague cuts a corner on the experience to hit a target?
options: Intervene straight away, without waiting for him
Let the numbers speak for themselves
Report it to him at the next review
Note it quietly for the annual appraisal
items.why: "intervene straight away — do not wait for me."

items.q: When Harry says "Clients cannot always articulate what they value — but they notice the moment it slips," he implies that…
options: clients are usually indifferent to service quality
the standard must be protected proactively, not just when clients complain
clients only care about speed of response
quality is best measured by direct client surveys
items.why: Inferência: se o cliente só percebe quando a qualidade cai, é preciso defendê-la antes, não reagir à reclamação.

items.q: How would you best describe Harry's stance in this session?
options: Anxious and resigned about losing the standard
Purposeful — he treats consistency as a shared responsibility
Indifferent to the human side of service
Focused mainly on cutting costs during the expansion
items.why: Inferência: ele delega a defesa do padrão a todos e dá instruções concretas — tom decidido, não resignado.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The firm's calm, unhurried service has become its signature." A signature here is…
options: a distinctive quality people recognise it by
items.why: Signature = assinatura, no sentido de marca distintiva pela qual algo é reconhecido.

items.q: "She handled the complaint with real discretion, never mentioning it again." Discretion means…
options: the judgement to be tactful and keep things private
items.why: Discretion = discrição: agir com tato e reserva.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Every ___ — the first call, the invoice, the follow-up email — shapes how the client sees us."
items.why: Touchpoint = ponto de contato: cada momento em que o cliente interage com a empresa.

items.q: "The best account managers embody the firm's values rather than merely quoting them." To embody means to…
options: represent something in how you actually behave
items.why: To embody = encarnar: personificar um valor pela própria conduta.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "An advantage that is genuinely ___ over many years is far harder for a rival to erode."
items.why: Sustained = sustentado: mantido de forma constante ao longo do tempo.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs de negócios ligados ao tema. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the new service standards." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new onboarding tone office by office." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on cutting the response-time standard." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar de algo proposto.

items.q: "They promised a personal follow-up but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi prometido.

items.q: "A faster chatbot alone won't move the needle on how clients feel about us." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, produzir diferença perceptível.
